p: Bodnant was founded in the 1870s by Henry Pochin, a Victorian industrial chemist, and his descendants, the McLaren family, carried on developing it before giving it to the National Trust in 1949. Over the generations they sponsored plant hunters who brought back seeds from all over the world, which is why the garden holds such an incredible range of trees and shrubs.

Its most famous feature is the Laburnum Arch, a long tunnel of golden flowers that drips with yellow blooms for a few weeks around late May and early June. It's a huge draw, so arrive early to walk through before the crowds. On the terraces, look out for the Pin Mill, an elegant old building that was moved here from Gloucestershire, standing at the end of the long canal pool. Down in the Dell, the River Hiraethlyn tumbles through woodland past an old mill, a cool, shady escape on warm days.
Allow at least three hours to explore properly. There's a café and shop near the entrance for a well-earned brew.

North Wales is packed with nearby treats. Conwy, with its mighty castle and town walls, is just down the valley. Llandudno, with its pier and the Great Orme, is a short drive along the coast. In Colwyn Bay, the Welsh Mountain Zoo sits on the hillside above the town, and the promenade from Porth Eirias towards Rhos-on-Sea is lovely for a seaside stroll and an ice cream.
